To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the developed methods and algorithms allow solar powered UAVs to perform robust, versatile and autonomous multi day continuous flights.

the energetic robustness and ease of use of solar powered UAVs can be significantly increased by: 1) using a formal design method which is based on energetic system models, 2) employing robust attitude estimation and control algorithms, 3) fusing thermal updraft tracking with solar powered flight, and 4) using a novel environment aware navigation framework for low altitude solar UAVs.

the development of novel algorithms, models, design methods and aerial systems for low altitude solar powered UAVs with the goal of enabling multi day continuous flight in complex real life scenarios.
the design of low altitude solarpowered UAVs for multi day continuous flight and environment aware autonomous navigation.
the development of a novel aerial system for robust low altitude perpetual flight in complex environments.

we have shown that low altitude solar powered UAVs can be made energetically robust, easy to use and versatile.
the contributions of this thesis allow solar powered UAVs to become more versatile, easier to operate and more energetically robust.
the presented contributions improve the energetic robust ness of solar powered UAVs and their ease of use, while simultaneously increasing their versatility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this thesis contributes to the development of a new class of aerial systems which are capable to perform large scale aerial sensing in a fully autonomous and robust manner.

we developed a novel framework for the environment aware autonomous navigation of solar UAVs in complex environments: We first present a novel approach for the fully autonomous detection of thermal updraft regions and the estimation of their thermal updraft strength.
the developed algorithms allow the autonomous navigation of solar powered UAVs in large scale aerial missions in complex environments such as forests or urban areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environment aware navigation of UAVs in complex environments is a highly challenging problem.
solar powered UAVs are a promising technology for large scale aerial sensing applications.

the navigation problem of low altitude solar UAVs is significantly more difficult than previously considered: The flight dynamics and the environment dependent energy consumption of solar UAVs are highly nonlinear, and the UAV's flight altitude is significantly smaller than for traditional aircraft.
